Nil T2 vs a Loss T2

A nil year had no activity, so no loss arises. A loss year had real expenses exceeding real revenue. Only one of them is a nil return.

Quick Answer

A nil year and a loss year are not the same thing, and only one of them is a nil return. A nil year had no activity at all, so net income is nil and no loss arises. A loss year had real expenses exceeding real revenue, which creates a non-capital loss to carry forward twenty years. A corporation that claims expenses is not nil, so a loss year is not covered by this service: it is prepared by Gondaliya CPA Professional Corporation at gondaliyacpa.ca at $350.00 plus HST per year. The quiet year is $300.00 plus HST per tax year.

Written and reviewed by Sharad Gondaliya, CPA (Ontario), CPA Ontario Membership 61040184.

Last reviewed: November 5, 2026

A Quiet Year Produces No Loss

These two are often confused, and the confusion is reasonable: both years end with no tax to pay. They get there differently. A nil year had no revenue, no expenses, no income of any kind and no disposition of property, so net income is nil and there is nothing to carry anywhere.

A loss year had real figures that went the wrong way. Expenses exceeded revenue, which creates a non-capital loss, and that loss is an asset of a kind: it can be carried twenty years forward or three years back against income in another year.

That is also why the two are priced differently. A corporation that claims expenses is not nil, so a loss year is not what this service files. It is prepared at gondaliyacpa.ca at $350.00 plus HST per year, and we say so before anything is charged.

Six rows differ and two do not. The two that do not are the mechanics both years share: pools and continuity run forwards either way. What separates them is simpler than the schedules suggest. A nil year had no activity at all, so net income is nil and no loss arises. A loss year had real expenses exceeding real revenue, which creates a non-capital loss to carry forward.

This comparison sets two of our own filing routes against each other and names no other provider. Where a comparison on this site does name one, it states that provider’s published prices and published features only.

What the Two Schedules Actually Carry

The numbering is the part most easily got wrong, because the two schedules are filed together and spoken of as one:

  • Schedule 8 is the capital cost allowance schedule. It records the corporation’s depreciable property, the class each asset sits in, and how much depreciation is claimed for the year.
  • Loss continuity is reported on Schedule 4, Corporation Loss Continuity and Application, not on Schedule 8.
  • Capital cost allowance is discretionary. A corporation may claim anything from nil up to the maximum the class allows, and the choice is made each year.
  • On a nil year the usual answer is to claim nil, because claiming against no income creates a non-capital loss, and a non-capital loss expires.
  • Leaving the claim unmade keeps the undepreciated capital cost in the pool, where it lasts indefinitely while the pool exists.
  • A non-capital loss is the ordinary kind, from expenses exceeding revenue, and runs twenty years forward and three years back. A net capital loss comes from selling capital property for less than it cost, and carries forward indefinitely.
  • A year that was never filed is a gap in the record, so the continuity has to be rebuilt before the later years can be assessed correctly.

A corporation that claims expenses is not nil. This service is for a corporation with no activity in the tax year; a loss year is prepared by Gondaliya CPA Professional Corporation at gondaliyacpa.ca at $350.00 plus HST per year.

It has depreciable property, so Schedule 8 is in play even though nothing happened. Claiming capital cost allowance against no income would create a non-capital loss, and that loss expires twenty years later; claiming nil keeps the undepreciated capital cost in the pool, where it lasts as long as the pool does. Frequently Asked Questions

Is a nil year the same as a loss year?

No. A nil year had no activity, so net income is nil and no loss arises. A loss needs real expenses exceeding real revenue.

Do you file a loss year?

No. A corporation that claims expenses is not nil. A loss year is prepared by Gondaliya CPA Professional Corporation at gondaliyacpa.ca at $350.00 plus HST per year.

Can I claim my expenses on a nil return to create a loss?

A year with expenses in it is not a nil year. Claiming them makes the return a loss return, which is a different service at a different price.

How long does a non-capital loss last?

Twenty years forward and three years back. A net capital loss carries forward indefinitely and back three years.

Which schedule carries the losses?

Schedule 4, Corporation Loss Continuity and Application. Schedule 8 is the capital cost allowance schedule, and the two are filed together, which is why they are often spoken of as one.

Does a nil year need Schedule 8 at all?

Only where the corporation holds depreciable property. One that still has equipment, a vehicle or a computer from its trading days does, even in a year when nothing happened.

Should I claim capital cost allowance on a quiet year?

Usually nil. Claiming against no income creates a non-capital loss that expires, while claiming nothing keeps the undepreciated capital cost in the pool, where it does not.

Is that choice fixed for good?

No. Capital cost allowance is discretionary and the choice is made each year, anywhere from nil up to the maximum the class allows.

What happens to the pool if I claim nothing?

It stays. The undepreciated capital cost remains in the pool indefinitely, while the pool exists, and carries forward to a future year.

Are Schedule 4 and Schedule 8 included in your fee?

Yes, where the corporation has anything to record on them. Both are inside $300.00 plus HST per tax year.

What does an unfiled year do to the continuity?

It leaves a gap in the record. The losses and pools have no filed return carrying them forward, so the continuity has to be rebuilt before the later years can be assessed correctly.

Why are several years filed oldest first?

Because continuity only runs forwards. Each return’s closing balances are the next one’s opening balances.

Can a corporation have nil years and loss years mixed together?

Yes. Each tax year is assessed on its own, so a quiet year and a trading year that lost money can sit side by side in the same catch-up.

What if I am not sure which kind of year I had?

Any revenue, any expense, income of any kind or a disposition of property takes the year out of nil. The amount is irrelevant to that test.

Which tool should I run first?

The loss continuity checker, which takes what carries forward on a quiet year.
